subject: Pilot economics & feature CAC mapping — Acme Health discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot economics & feature CAC mapping — Acme Health discovery follow-up

Tom — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and the asks we walked through on the call: 

- Confirmed pilot scope: conversational summarization + clinical note generation for a subset of end users (approx 200 active pilot users).
- Baseline traffic you shared: ~1.2M generation tokens / month (90% chat), ~150k embedding tokens / month, spikes up to ~2.5M tokens in month-over-month tests.
- Pilot objectives: validate user value and establish per-feature economics to inform paid roll-out.
- Your stated constraints: prefer CAC payback <= 9 months, initial pilot budget cap ~$40k/year; target per-1M-token cost in the ballpark of low-mid hundreds (you mentioned $300–$500 as acceptable).

Ask from Redwood: can you confirm the steady-state monthly active users for the pilot (you mentioned 200 but said it could be 150–250)? Also confirm whether we should model a 6-mo or 9-mo CAC payback target for pricing scenarios.

Next steps we propose:
- We’ll produce a short feature-level profitability model that maps tokens -> $/1M tokens -> suggested price per feature -> CAC payback timeline (spreadsheet attached).
- Internal alignment on whether we position the pilot as hosted (consumption) or dedicated (reserved) for pricing and cost estimates.
- 30-min follow-up to review the model and SOW draft (suggest Wed or Thu this week).

I’ve attached a working token model (acme_pilot_token_model.xlsx) and a brief Redwood pricing snapshot to show ranges. If you prefer a targeted number for $/1M tokens up front, we can aim the first pass at $400/1M as a conservative midpoint and show a sensitivity band +/- 50%.

Thanks — looking forward to your confirmation on the MAU and preferred payback horizon.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot economics & feature CAC mapping — Acme Health discovery follow-up

Putting a quick back-of-envelope together before we build the spreadsheet Stephanie attached. Assumptions / coarse numbers to include in the model: 

- Inference cost range (per 1M tokens):
  - Optimized quantized path (Llama-style 7B / runtime optimizations): ~$300/1M tokens
  - Medium model (13B, mixed-precision): ~$650/1M tokens
  - Larger model or unquantized (70B / high-latency batch): ~$1,100/1M tokens

- For Acme pilot (1.2M gen tokens/month): monthly inference cost range ~ $360 (quantized) -> $1,320 (larger model). Embedding cost negligible relative but include $25–$75/month.

- Feature mapping (example):
  - "Clinical Summaries" per active user: ~55k tokens/mo -> cost per active user/month = 0.055 * $/1M. At $400/1M tokens that's ~$22/user/month inference cost.
  - "Note Generation" (longer outputs): ~220k tokens/mo -> ~$88/user/month at $400/1M.

- Pricing suggestions to hit margin targets (target gross margin 60–70%):
  - If expected inference cost per user for a feature = C, price P should be ~ C / (1 - margin). Example: if C = $22 and margin target = 65%, P ≈ $63/user/month.

- CAC payback illustration: if average contract value (first-year ARR per acquired account) = $750, and CAC = $1,800 (example), payback months = CAC / (monthly gross margin contribution). We should request Acme’s expected LTV or new-account economics to get accurate payback months.

I’ll fill the spreadsheet with three scenarios (conservative / midpoint / aggressive) and include a row-level calculation for price per feature, implied margin, and payback months. Suggest we show a 'pilot-first' SKU with a 20–30% transient discount to accelerate trial-to-paid conversion — that will change payback math but is often necessary.

Attaching a draft token model (acme_pilot_token_model.xlsx) — will iterate after Tom confirms MAU and payback target.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot economics & feature CAC mapping — Acme Health discovery follow-up

Thanks Ben — a couple notes from a GTM / approval perspective before we lock numbers: 

- If Acme’s stated budget cap is ~$40k/year for the pilot, we need to be explicit about what that covers (inference-only vs. product+implementation). Recommend we propose: inference consumption up to X tokens + one integration sprint (up to 20 engineer hours) bundled.
- For commercial approval: aim for a midpoint list price per feature that yields ~65% gross margin at the projected inference cost. If that means listing price looks higher, we can present a temporary pilot discount (30% off list) — the sales math needs to show payback horizon under 9 months when conversion rate assumptions are included.
- Legal/procurement note: they will want a short SOW + standard data processing addendum. Ask procurement for preferred contract start/end dates; that impacts our recognition and pilot billing.

Action items for this thread:
- Ben: finalize the three-scenario tab (conservative/mid/aggressive) and include a column that shows required conversion rate to achieve <=9-month CAC payback.
- Stephanie: confirm MAU range (150–250) and whether the $40k figure is pilot-only or pilot+implementation.
- I’ll pre-draft a short SOW template that ties pricing to indexed token bands so we don’t have to renegotiate during pilot spikes.

Laura Bennett
Director, GTM Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot economics & feature CAC mapping — Acme Health discovery follow-up

Stephanie — thanks for the clear summary and Ben/Laura for the numbers. Confirming for the record:

- MAU for the pilot: 200 steady-state (we can scale to 250 if the first month looks good).
- Budget: $40k/year pilot cap — that should include inference + one implementation block (we’ll accept up to 25 hours of integration support). Anything beyond that we’ll discuss as change order.
- Preferred payback: we want to see a 6–9 month payback in the scenarios you share; 6 months is ideal, 9 months is acceptable.
- Target $/1M tokens: we’re comfortable seeing scenarios centered around $350–$450/1M tokens.

Please proceed with the three-scenario model centered on $400/1M, and include the pilot discount path Laura referenced. We’re happy to review a short SOW; send over a draft and we’ll route to procurement. I’ve attached our internal checklist (acme_contract_checklist.pdf) that procurement asked us to share.

Can we lock a 30-min review for Fri 10:00 AM PT? That time works for our team.

Best,
Tom Ellis
Head of Product, Acme Health
tom.ellis@acmehealth.com | +1 617-555-0123
